subject: Post-demo recap: throughput, latency and reserved capacity sizing
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Rivers <tim.rivers@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: throughput, latency and reserved capacity sizing

Hi Tim —

Thanks for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we landed on so we’re aligned before we size a Dedicated pilot: 

1) Target SLOs you called out
   - P95 latency target: 120ms for single-shot generation (avg prompt length ~ 120 tokens)
   - Streaming/RT mode: start-of-token latency under 70ms; tail behavior P99 < 300ms
2) Throughput & concurrency
   - Peak concurrency expected: 450 concurrent requests during 30m bursts
   - Steady-state QPS (generation requests): ~110 qps
3) Quality & model variant
   - You want to validate open-model-2-14B quantized (nf4/8) with a fallback to 7B optimized for latency
4) Data & security notes
   - Pilot must run in Dedicated (customer-owned VPC) with audit logging to your SIEM

Next steps we agreed on:
- We’ll propose a reserved throughput configuration (vGPU mix + reserved token throughput) for a 4-week validation pilot.
- Internal SE (Ben) to provide a GPU comparison table and expected concurrency headroom for the suggested configs.
- You to confirm representative prompt set and a short spike window date so we can pre-warm KV caches and run a smoke pilot.

Attachments: I attached a quick sizing sheet that Ben will fill with GPU options and expected qps/headroom.

Proposed timeline: provisioning within 5 business days after sign-off; pilot window target next week (let me know if Wed 8/18 or Thu 8/19 works).

Thanks — looking forward.

—SoJin
Soojin Lee
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0123
From: Tim Rivers <tim.rivers@novusai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: throughput, latency and reserved capacity sizing

Thanks Soojin — solid notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

• The 450 concurrent requests is simultaneous active sessions during a campaign spike; most sessions are short (1–2 exchanges).
• The 110 qps steady-state is a conservative daytime average — offline batch will be scheduled separately.
• For streaming, we care most about first-byte latency for interactive agents; steady streaming token cadence can be lower.

We’ll pull together a representative prompt set (50 prompts spanning 30–250 tokens) by EOD tomorrow.

Wed 8/18 works better for us for the spike test if you can provision by then. Also can you add a quick note on expected memory/KV cache footprint per session for the 14B variant? That will help our infra team size the VPC endpoints and egress rules.

—Tim
Tim Rivers
Head of Platform Engineering, NovusAI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Tim Rivers <tim.rivers@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: throughput, latency and reserved capacity sizing

Tim / Soojin — attaching the initial GPU comparison and a filled sizing sheet (xlsx) — high level notes below. Attachment: gpu-comparison-notes.pdf, redwood-dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx (see tab "pilot_reco").

Summary recommendations for pilot (4-week):
1) Config A — 4x A10G (mixed-precision optimized)
   - Expected single-shot p95: ~85–110ms at 110 qps with 64-token responses (14B quantized nf4/8)
   - Streaming latency first-byte: ~45–60ms under steady-state
   - Concurrency headroom: good for 300–350 active sessions without aggressive batching
   - Cost: mid-range; easier fit for pre-emptible clouds
2) Config B — 2x A100 40GB + 2x A10G
   - Better headroom for KV cache-heavy workflows and multi-turn state (p95 similar to A10G-only but P99 improved)
   - Higher cost, lower frequency scaling pain for spikes
3) Config C — 8x lower-memory GPUs (T4 / equivalent) in a sharded setup
   - Cheaper but increased tail latency and higher operational complexity for streaming
Memory/KV notes (per active session, 14B quantized):
- Cold KV footprint: ~7–9MB per session (depends on cached prefixes)
- Active working set when generating: peak ~60–120MB depending on sequence length
Pilot reservation: recommend starting with Config A and reserve an extra 20% burst capacity for the scheduled spike (so reserve throughput to handle ~140 qps peak sustained for 10m, 450 concurrent session headroom handled by burst pool).
Action items I put in the sheet: exact provision counts per availability zone, pre-warm commands, and smoke test checklist. I can iterate after you drop the prompt set.
—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Rivers <tim.rivers@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-13T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: throughput, latency and reserved capacity sizing

Thanks Ben — that aligns with what I expected. Tim, two small follow-ups so we can lock the pilot config: 

A) Can you confirm the average expected response length for the 50 prompt set (approx tokens out)? That changes token-throttling and reserved token throughput calculations.
B) For the pilot we’ll provision Config A with a 20% burst pool as Ben suggested. We’ll expose an ops endpoint for pre-warm and a tracing hook so your infra can ingest P95/P99.

If you’re good with Config A, I’ll send a pilot statement of work and provisioning request today and we’ll aim to have capacity ready by Mon 8/16 to run a smoke test and then the spike on Wed 8/18.

Also attaching the HubSpot deal link and a short DocuSign placeholder so legal can sign the pilot terms quickly.

—SoJin
From: Tim Rivers <tim.rivers@novusai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: throughput, latency and reserved capacity sizing

Appreciate the summary and the attachments. Quick answers: 
• Representative prompts ready — average response length ~58 tokens, 90th percentile 140 tokens. I uploaded the prompt set to the Drive link you sent.
• Confirm Config A + 20% burst pool — please proceed with provisioning. We’ll provide credentials for VPC peering and a short runbook for our SIEM ingestion.

Schedule: Smoke test Mon 8/16 09:00 PT; Spike test Wed 8/18 13:00 PT (30m). I’ll invite our infra team to both runs.

Please go ahead and send the pilot SoW/DocuSign; Ben — if you can include a short section on how we’ll measure KV cache warm-up impact on latency, that would be helpful.

—Tim
